lessons.title: Introduction to Coroutines
lessons.content: Coroutines are lightweight, suspendable computations letting you write async code sequentially. Real scenario: fetching from three APIs and combining results without a callback pyramid.

lessons.title: suspend Functions
lessons.content: The suspend modifier marks a function that can pause without blocking the thread, callable only from another suspend function or a coroutine. Real scenario: a repository's network call callable directly from a ViewModel coroutine.

lessons.title: Coroutine Builders Overview
lessons.content: launch, async, runBlocking are the main ways to start a coroutine, each suited to different cases. Real scenario: launch for fire-and-forget saves, async when you need a result to await later.

codeSnippets.code:
viewModelScope.launch { saveData() }
val deferred = viewModelScope.async { fetchData() }

lessons.title: launch Builder
lessons.content: launch starts a coroutine returning a Job, no result - used for side-effecting work. Real scenario: launching a coroutine to persist a settings change without blocking the UI thread.

lessons.title: async / await
lessons.content: async returns a Deferred<T> for concurrent work, retrieved later with .await() without blocking a thread. Real scenario: fetching a user and posts in parallel, roughly halving load time.

lessons.title: Job
lessons.content: A Job represents a cancellable unit of work, tracking a coroutine's lifecycle and forming parent-child hierarchies. Real scenario: storing a Job to cancel a specific long upload individually.

codeSnippets.code:
val uploadJob = viewModelScope.launch { uploadLargeFile() }
fun cancelUpload() { uploadJob.cancel() }

lessons.title: Deferred
lessons.content: Deferred<T> is a Job that also holds a future result, returned by async - Kotlin's equivalent of a Future/Promise. Real scenario: kicking off async work early and awaiting the result once other setup completes.

codeSnippets.code:
val deferredUser = viewModelScope.async { fetchUser() }
val user = deferredUser.await()

lessons.title: Coroutine Dispatchers Overview
lessons.content: A Dispatcher decides which thread(s) a coroutine runs on: Main, IO, Default, Unconfined. Real scenario: switching a network call to IO and the UI update back to Main.

lessons.title: Dispatchers.Main
lessons.content: Runs coroutines on the UI thread, required for touching Views or Compose state. Real scenario: viewModelScope defaults to Main.immediate, letting you update StateFlow directly.

lessons.title: Dispatchers.IO
lessons.content: Optimized for blocking I/O with a larger thread pool since I/O threads mostly wait rather than compute. Real scenario: running a Room query or network call wrapped in withContext(Dispatchers.IO).

lessons.title: Dispatchers.Default
lessons.content: Optimized for CPU-intensive work, sized to CPU core count. Real scenario: parsing a very large JSON payload dispatched to Default instead of the main thread.

lessons.title: Dispatchers.Unconfined
lessons.content: Starts in the caller's thread but isn't confined after suspension - mostly for library internals/testing, generally not recommended for app code. Real scenario: recognizing it in test utilities, avoiding it in business logic.

codeSnippets.code:
// generally avoid in app code
GlobalScope.launch(Dispatchers.Unconfined) { delay(100) }

lessons.title: CoroutineScope
lessons.content: Defines the lifecycle boundary for coroutines - cancelling the scope cancels every coroutine launched in it. Real scenario: viewModelScope tied to the ViewModel, auto-cancelling on clear.

lessons.title: SupervisorJob
lessons.content: Prevents one child's failure from cancelling siblings, unlike a regular Job. Real scenario: a dashboard fetching 4 widgets where one API failing shouldn't take down the others.

codeSnippets.code: val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main)

lessons.title: supervisorScope
lessons.content: The structured-concurrency-friendly way to get SupervisorJob semantics for a specific block. Real scenario: loading independent screen sections in parallel where each fails gracefully on its own.

lessons.title: Structured Concurrency Principles
lessons.content: Every coroutine has a clear parent scope and can't outlive it, eliminating leaked background work as a bug category. Real scenario: a coroutineScope block guaranteeing all children finish or cancel together.

lessons.title: Coroutine Cancellation
lessons.content: Cancellation is cooperative - a coroutine must check for it to actually stop, which suspend functions do automatically. Real scenario: a computation loop checking ensureActive() periodically.

lessons.title: Timeouts: withTimeout / withTimeoutOrNull
lessons.content: withTimeout throws on expiry; withTimeoutOrNull returns null instead, often more convenient. Real scenario: a 10s network timeout falling back to cached data.

codeSnippets.code: val result = withTimeoutOrNull(10_000) { fetchFromNetwork() } ?: loadFromCache()

lessons.title: Exception Handling in Coroutines
lessons.content: launch propagates exceptions to the parent immediately; async defers them until await(). CoroutineExceptionHandler catches uncaught top-level exceptions. Real scenario: an exception in async 'disappearing' until await() is called.

codeSnippets.code:
val handler = CoroutineExceptionHandler { _, e -> Log.e("App", e.message ?: "") }
scope.launch(handler) { throw RuntimeException("oops") }

lessons.title: Mutex
lessons.content: Provides coroutine-safe mutual exclusion by suspending instead of blocking a thread. Real scenario: protecting a shared in-memory cache from concurrent coroutine writes.

lessons.title: Channel
lessons.content: A coroutine-safe queue for passing values between coroutines, both send and receive suspend. Real scenario: a producer coroutine sending sensor data to a separate consumer coroutine.

lessons.title: select Expression
lessons.content: Lets a coroutine wait on multiple suspending operations simultaneously, proceeding with whichever completes first. Real scenario: a sync worker reacting to whichever of two event channels fires first.

lessons.title: Actor Pattern (via Channel)
lessons.content: Encapsulates mutable state behind a message-processing coroutine, so all mutations happen sequentially, avoiding locks entirely. Real scenario: a single coroutine owning a counter, processed message by message.

lessons.title: Shared Mutable State: The Core Problem
lessons.content: Concurrent coroutines mutating the same variable without sync causes race conditions. Real scenario: ten coroutines incrementing a shared counter without sync producing a wrong final count - the classic demo.
